Cost Curves

This scene pulls marginal and average cost curves out of a total cost curve.

Marginal cost is the extra cost of making one more unit. Average cost is total cost divided by quantity. When one more unit costs less than the average, the average falls. So the marginal cost curve passes exactly through the lowest point of average cost.

For example, a 🏪 shop's average cost is 1,000 won per 🍞 bread loaf. Baking one more costs 800 won, so the average falls. At 1,200 won, the average rises instead. That is why marginal cost meets average cost at its lowest point.

MC(q)=C′(q),AC(q)=C(q)qMC(q) = C'(q), \quad AC(q) = \frac{C(q)}{q}MC(q)=C′(q),AC(q)=qC(q)​
